remedies.title: Break the Send/Reply cycle with a send hierarchy
remedies.rationale: QNX message passing is synchronous: a thread blocked in MsgSend() cannot receive. If two servers send to each other, each waits for the other to receive. QNX designs avoid this with a send hierarchy: messages only flow one way; the other direction uses non-blocking notifications (MsgSendPulse()/MsgDeliverEvent()) and the notified side pulls the data.
guidance: The trace shows the cycle fusion_a -> fusion_b -> fusion_a; these MsgSend() calls are where it closes.

Pick a direction (usually: the more central server never sends to its clients). On the other side, replace MsgSend() with MsgSendPulse() (or MsgDeliverEvent() from a reply), and let the receiver fetch what it needs with its own MsgSend() down the hierarchy.
Not automated: the reply carries data, so the new protocol is a design decision.

note: no root cause here has a safe automatic transform; apply the guidance, then compare
